title: Müller wins Misano Race 2 after Rast’s puncture
dek: Nico Müller won Misano Race 2 for Audi by 7.6 seconds from Philipp Eng after pole-sitter René Rast’s puncture, and Marco Wittmann’s race ended on lap one.

chapters.title: Wittmann’s win and a 100th race to come
text: Saturday at Misano had belonged to Marco Wittmann, who won Race 1 for BMW Team RMG after starting last, pitting at the end of the first lap and nursing one set of tyres to the flag. René Rast was second, 8.238 seconds behind, and Loïc Duval completed the podium, which left Rast as the points leader. BMW had put five cars in the top ten.

Sunday brought the same mandatory-stop format and a milestone for two BMW drivers: it was the 100th DTM race for both Wittmann and Timo Glock. With Race 1 decided by an early stop and a safety car, the question was whether the same gamble would pay twice.

chapters.title: Rast on pole again as Audi fills the first five places
text: Second qualifying was red-flagged three minutes in, when Andrea Dovizioso locked his brakes and became stuck in the gravel at Turn 13. The marshals pushed the Audi back on to the track, the session restarted with 16 minutes to go, and the first runs of the whole field were effectively wasted.

Rast took his second pole of the weekend with 1:25.384, 0.070 seconds ahead of Robin Frijns in the Abt Sportsline Audi. Jonathan Aberdein was on the verge of the front row but made a mistake in the second sector of his last lap and was third, about two tenths off the pace. Nico Müller was fourth, and Pietro Fittipaldi fifth, 0.275 seconds from pole, completing an Audi top five.

Wittmann, the winner on Saturday, was the best BMW in sixth, 0.380 seconds behind Rast, with Duval just three thousandths further back in seventh. Joel Eriksson, Philipp Eng and Timo Glock were eighth to tenth. Dovizioso recovered to 14th, while the four R-Motorsport Aston Martins filled the last four places on the grid, led by Jake Dennis in 15th. Rast said it had been a lot of pressure and work in the car, and that his last lap was not clean.

chapters.title: A three-wide fight at Turn 8 ends Wittmann’s race
text: Rast made a poor start from pole. Frijns went into the lead, Müller jumped from fourth to second, and Rast was squeezed between Müller and Aberdein. As he tried to recover places he ended up three abreast into Turn 8 with Aberdein and Wittmann, and Wittmann was pushed off the track. The BMW was damaged, including the steering, and he retired on the opening lap. The stewards took no action and the car was recovered without a safety car.

Others tried the early stop that had won Saturday’s race: Rockenfeller, Glock and Juncadella came in on the first lap, van der Linde a lap later. Glock’s BMW had a technical problem, and both he and Paul di Resta, who parked his Aston Martin in a Turn 13 escape road, were out within the first ten laps. Neither stoppage needed a safety car.

chapters.title: Rast takes the lead, then picks up a puncture
text: Rast then gained places quickly. He passed Müller for second on lap eight and Frijns for the lead a lap later, and began to open a gap. Müller took second from Frijns on lap ten, and Duval, who had passed Aberdein, tagged Frijns into a spin on lap 11. Duval was given a drive-through penalty for it. Eng, who had made a quick start from ninth on the grid, passed Aberdein for fourth on lap 13.
On lap 14 Rast picked up a puncture on the left rear, and had to limp back to the pits. Müller inherited the lead as the rest of the field worked through its stops.

chapters.title: Eng passes Rast, Müller passes Dennis
text: Eng stopped at the end of lap 16 and rejoined just behind Rast on cold tyres. Müller stopped from the lead a lap later and came out just ahead of Fittipaldi, who was the first of the stopped cars. Rast and Eng both passed Fittipaldi on lap 19. When the leaders reached the lapped Duval, Eng saw his chance and passed Rast for second on lap 21, going to the inside of the Audi at the Turn 10 hairpin.

Jake Dennis was the last driver yet to make his mandatory stop and was leading the race, with Müller closing quickly. The Audi driver took the lead from the Aston Martin on lap 25 and then managed the gap.

chapters.title: Müller clear by 7.6 seconds
text: Müller won by 7.628 seconds after 38 laps in 57:37.468, with Eng second and Rast third, 16.804 seconds back after flatspotting a front tyre. Frijns, who set the fastest lap on lap two, passed Fittipaldi for fourth on lap 35 and held him off to the line, 0.358 seconds ahead. Fittipaldi’s fifth place was his best DTM result.

Eriksson passed Aberdein for sixth on the last lap, and the Audi driver was seventh. Spengler was eighth after a duel with Dovizioso, van der Linde ninth and Rockenfeller tenth. Duval, with his penalty, was 11th. Ferdinand Habsburg was the best of the Aston Martins in 12th, ahead of Dennis. Dovizioso spun at Turn 16 late on, carrying too much speed over the kerb, and finished 15th after the Audi’s engine kept running.

chapters.title: Müller breaks a three-year wait as Rast extends his lead
text: It was Müller’s first win of the season and only his second in the DTM after the Norisring in 2016. He said he had worked for it for a long time, that a victory feels completely different from a podium, and that he believed he would have won even without Rast’s puncture. Audi Sport head Dieter Gass praised a strong start and a strong race, and Müller credited the RS 5 DTM with performing exceptionally well at Misano. He had been fifth in Saturday’s race despite struggling with tyre management, and said a top-five finish every weekend was the aim.

For BMW it was a weekend of highs and lows. Eng’s second place from ninth on the grid, with good overtakes and tyre management, was the highlight of the day for BMW Motorsport’s Rudolf Dittrich, who also lamented that Wittmann and Glock had both left their 100th races far too early. Wittmann was unhappy to be pushed out by the Audis and said the blow to his left front was hard enough to break the car; the contact was ruled a racing incident, and his Team RMG boss Stefan Reinhold felt he would likely have been on the podium. BMW had four cars in the top ten, after five on Saturday. Eng himself said there was no guarantee of finishing second from ninth on the grid, and that with good tyres he might have pushed earlier to attack Müller; he also wanted the team to check whether his DRS had worked every time. Spengler said that climbing from 13th to eighth without incidents such as a safety car was a good result.

Rast, on the podium in both races, left Misano still leading. The standings read Rast 93 points, Eng 83, Müller 76 and Wittmann 68. Duval’s drive-through penalty left him 11th, and Dovizioso, who spun late on, was 15th, the last of the classified runners.

The DTM now had a break of almost four weeks before the Norisring on 5–7 July. Müller said Audi had been stronger at Misano and BMW at Zolder, but saw no reason his team’s pace should differ at Nuremberg, while warning that the street circuit always brings surprises.

facts.v: Müller won by 7.628 seconds, his second DTM victory after the Norisring in 2016.
